claim_text: Barring any black swan events, ETH will break through its previous all-time high of around $4,875, after which it enters price discovery with no historical resistance overhead and should move rapidly higher.
ETH's base case target for 2025 is around $7,300 (a little over $7,000), roughly double its current price.
In the most extreme bullish scenario taken seriously for 2025, ETH could rise to around $14,000 (about 3.65x its current price), acting as a practical upper limit.
BTC's plausible upper ceiling for 2025 is around $200,000, but a figure well below $200,000 is considered more likely to actually occur.

The analyst's base case is that the United States will fall into a recession (defined as two negative quarters of real GDP) at some point in 2025, contradicting the White House claim that a recession is '100% not' going to happen — though he stresses this is not currently happening yet and is a probability, not a certainty.
The US economy will avoid falling into a recession over the next roughly five months, through October 2025, despite the earlier yield curve inversion signal.
The bull market in US stocks resumes and continues heading into the end of 2025.
QQQ will continue to underperform SCHD for a while, and if QQQ rises about 20% by year-end, SCHD would likely rise only around 8-10% in comparison.
The analyst will eventually buy and dollar-cost-average into QQQ, even though he considers current valuations unattractive.
SCHD remains a suitable holding to continue buying/dollar-cost-averaging into now, rather than selling, despite being down year-to-date.

Over the long term the S&P 500 will keep climbing the 'wall of worry' absent a sufficient reason not to, making dollar-cost-averaging into low expense ratio index funds the best long-term strategy rather than trying to time the market.
The S&P 500's recent pullback is a short-term correction driven by the long end of the yield curve (10-year yield) rising, and further yield increases would extend this correction.
The 10-year yield will likely continue rallying into early January 2025, potentially topping around then, mimicking the 2016 pattern where yields and the dollar rallied hard in Q4 before topping out.
Once the 10-year yield tops out, the S&P 500 should resume its rally, similar to how it bottomed in October 2023 right after the 10-year yield topped.
TLT will likely form a double bottom (or sweep the prior low) before attempting a rally, but historically such bounces often still resolve lower afterward.
There is a risk the current S&P 500 pullback evolves into a larger ~20% correction, similar to what happened in 1996, which would also be detrimental to the crypto market.
The US economy is not currently in a recessionary environment, and will not be considered one unless initial jobless claims rise to around 300k.
Gold will not fall back to $1500 or even $3000; it will likely reach $3500-$4000 before the end of the year and go much higher after that.
Gold mining stocks could double or triple between now and the end of the year as they get repriced to reflect gold's higher price.
The US is heading into serious economic trouble as its unsustainable deficits and reliance on foreign capital finally catch up with it, undermining the dollar and US debt.
Bitcoin's 2025 bear case price target is $150,000
Bitcoin's 2025 base case price target is $225,000
Bitcoin's 2025 bull case price target is $400,000
Solana will have a good year in 2025
Bitcoin is bottoming out after its recent pullback and the broader bull market will resume upward from here
Real estate prices are tanking fast and this represents a good buying opportunity, particularly between Thanksgiving and the end of January
Microsoft will remain one of the most durable, predictable, and growing companies for a lifetime, making it the best long-term buy-and-hold stock compared to Apple or Google.
Costco is uniquely positioned as a company that can be held for a lifetime, more so than Walmart or Target.
Berkshire Hathaway is virtually indestructible and is likely to survive and be worth holding for a lifetime.
S&P Global is the best long-term buy-and-hold stock among dominant-moat data/ratings companies (versus FICO and ASML) and is unlikely to be disrupted over the next 30 years.
Visa is the most likely of the major payment networks (versus Mastercard and American Express) to be a lifelong buy-and-hold, with growth sustained for at least the next 20 years.

The Magnificent 7/AI stocks are currently in a bubble-like state similar to the 1999 dot-com bubble, and if their earnings don't grow enough to justify current valuations, these stocks face a significant price correction/re-rating downward.

Nvidia's current ~50x P/E multiple prices in the market's assumption that it will remain in business for decades, keep growing profits, and won't be supplanted by competitors — an assumption that is not guaranteed to hold, and if it fails, the stock's valuation will be repriced downward.

The S&P 500 is at risk of a significant future correction similar in nature to the 2000 dot-com crash, due to its unprecedented concentration in a handful of highly valued mega-cap stocks, though the exact timing and magnitude cannot be predicted.
Palantir stock will reach at least $500 per share within 5 years on the bear case, with a conservative bullish target of about $1,000 per share.
In the short term, Palantir's stock is overstretched and hyped, driven partly by FOMO, and could be due for a pullback.
By around 2027, Palantir's PE ratio will have compressed to about 40x while the share price will be around $300.
